question.problem:
An economist measured $4$ particular features, ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4},$ for each currency in a collection under devaluation. The collected data was stored in the standardized observation matrix $X,$ where each row contains measurements for a particular currency.
The singular values of $X$ are 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}=12,\,{\sigma }_{2}=7,\,{\sigma }_{3}=3,\,{\sigma }_{4}=1.
$$

The economist then converted the original observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ using the equation $Y=X{V}_{1},$ where ${V}_{1}$ is the $4\times 1$ matrix consisting of the first principal component of the data. What percentage of the original variance is preserved in the new transformed matrix $Y$ compared to the initial observation matrix $X?$
